title: The Saráís Act, 1867
purpose: to provide for the regulation of public Saráí s and Puraos
scope: This Act applies to public Saráís and Puraos, initially extending to the territories under the government of the Lieutenant Governor of the North-West Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal. The State Government may extend it to other parts of its territories, except the towns of Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay. Section 8 applies to all Saráís, but no other part of the Act applies to any Saráí under the direct management of the State Government or any Municipal Committee.
key_provisions: Section 3 & 5: The Magistrate of the District shall give written notice to keepers of Saráís, requiring them to register. After one month from such notice, keepers shall not receive lodgers or allow animals/vehicles until the Saráí and keeper's name/residence are registered.
Section 7(1): The keeper of a Saráí shall give immediate notice to the nearest police-station if any person in the Saráí is ill of an infectious or contagious disease, or dies of such disease.

Section 7(3): The keeper of a Saráí shall thoroughly cleanse the rooms, verandahs, drains, wells, tanks, or other water sources of the Saráí to the satisfaction of and as often as required by the Magistrate of the District or his appointee.

Section 7(6): The keeper of a Saráí shall provide such number of watchmen as may, in the opinion of the Magistrate of the District (subject to State Government rules), be necessary for the safety and protection of persons, animals, or vehicles lodging in, halting at, or placed in the Saráí.

Section 8: The keeper of a Saráí shall, if required by an order of the Magistrate of the District, report (orally or in writing) to the Magistrate or his appointee every person who resorted to the Saráí during the preceding day or night. Schedules for written reports exceeding a single day/night shall be furnished by the Magistrate.

Section 14: If the keeper of a Saráí offends against any provision of this Act or its regulations, they shall be liable on conviction before any Magistrate to a penalty not exceeding twenty rupees, and a further penalty not exceeding one Rupee a day for every day the offence continues. Penalties are recoverable as fines under the Code of Criminal Procedure.
administration: The Magistrate of the District is responsible for giving notice of the Act, keeping registers of Saráís and their keepers, refusing registration, ensuring keepers fulfill their duties (e.g., cleanliness, watchmen), ordering reports from keepers, managing deserted or ruinous Saráís, and enforcing penalties. The State Government has the power to direct the form and signatories for certificates of character, prescribe rules for watchmen, and make regulations for the better attainment of the Act's objects, which must be published in the official Gazette.

title: THE NORTH -WESTERN PROVINCES AND OUDH ACT, 1890
purpose: To provide for the better administration of the North -Western Provinces and Oudh and to amend certain enactments in force in those Provinces and in Oudh, specifically to provide for the better administration of the territories respectively administered by the Lieutenant Governor of the North -Western Provinces and the Chief Commissioner of Oudh.
scope: The territories administered by the Lieutenant Governor of the North -Western Provinces (including the Jhansi Division, comprising the districts of Jhansi, Jalaun and Lalatpur, annexed to the Allahabad Division) and the territories administered by the Chief Commissioner of Oudh.
key_provisions: Section 5 (1): All enactments in force in the temporarily-settled districts of the Allahabad Division and not in the Jhansi Division shall be deemed to come into force in the Jhansi Division on and from the day Part I commences.

Section 5 (2): All enactments in force in the Jhansi Division and not in the temporarily-settled districts, including the Jhansi Courts Act, 1867 (18 of 1867), and Act No. 27 of 1867, shall be deemed to be repealed on and from the day Part I commences, with the exception of the Jhansi Encumbered Estates Act, 1882 (16 of 1882) and the Jhansi and Morar Act, 1886 (17 of 1886).

Section 7: Functions assigned to the Deputy Commissioner and the Commissioner by the Jhansi and Morar Act, 1886 (17 of 1886), shall be discharged by the District Judge and the High Court, respectively. References to Courts in the Jhansi district subordinate to the Commissioner shall apply to Civil Courts established under the Bengal, North -Western Provinces and Assam Civil Courts Act, 1887 (12 of 1887).

Section 9 (2): All cases or proceedings pending in any Civil Court in the Jhansi division on the day Part I commences shall be disposed of as follows: by the Munsif (if pending in the Court of a Tahsildar or of an Assistant Commissioner of the second class), by the Subordinate Judge (if pending in the Court of an Assistant Commissioner of the first class), by the District Judge (if pending in the Court of a Deputy Commissioner or the Commissioner, unless an appeal from a decree or order of the Deputy Commissioner, in which case the appeal shall be disposed of by the High Court).

Section 11 (1): The Board of Revenue constituted under the North -Western Provinces Land -revenue Act, 1873 (19 of 1873), shall also be the Board of Revenue for the territories administered by the Chief Commissioner of Oudh, known and designated as the Board of Revenue of the North -Western Provinces and Oudh, and shall be the Chief Revenue-authority in Oudh.

Section 63 (1): The Board of Revenue of the North -Western Provinces and Oudh shall, for the disposal of cases under the Oudh Rent Act, 1886 (22 of 1886), sit in such place or places in the North -Western Provinces or Oudh as the State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.
administration: The Act is administered by various authorities depending on the specific part or function. Commencement of Part I is directed by the Lieutenant Governor, Part II by the Chief Commissioner of Oudh, and Part III by the Lieutenant Governor of the North -Western Provinces and Chief Commissioner of Oudh, all by notification in the Official Gazette. Functions assigned by the Jhansi and Morar Act, 1886, are discharged by the District Judge and the High Court. Pending cases in Civil Courts in the Jhansi division are disposed of by the Munsif, Subordinate Judge, District Judge, and High Court. The Board of Revenue of the North -Western Provinces and Oudh acts as the Board of Revenue and Chief Revenue-authority in Oudh and disposes of cases. The State Government may transfer pending appeals to the District Judge and appoint the sitting places for the Board of Revenue.

title: THE TOBACCO DUTY (TOWN OF BOMBAY) ACT, 1857
purpose: To amend the law relating to the duties payable on Tobacco, and the retail sale and warehousing thereof in the Town of Bombay.
scope: This Act applies to all Tobacco (except small quantities for private consumption) imported into, removed within, or sold by retail in the Town of Bombay (including the Islands of Bombay and Colaba), and covers the duties, retail sale, and warehousing of Tobacco.
key_provisions: Section II: All Tobacco imported into the Town of Bombay and intended for consumption therein shall be liable to a Municipal Duty of seven Rupees and eight annas per maund of forty seers of eighty tolas to the seer, in addition to any Customs Duty.

Section IX: It shall not be lawful to remove any Tobacco from one place to another within the Town, or carry it on any thoroughfare or in certain vessels, without a Permit from the Commissioner of Customs Salt and Opium. This Permit shall be in the form of Schedule A and is valid only between sunrise and sunset of the day for which it is granted.

Section XI: No person shall sell or offer for sale by retail any Tobacco in the Town without a license from the Commissioner of Customs, Salt and Opium. The license is valid for twelve calendar months from its date, and a fee of one Rupee must be paid for each license.

Section XIV: Every retail dealer in Tobacco must, on or before the tenth day of each month, submit a separate return to the Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium for each licensed shop, detailing the quantity of Tobacco on hand at the beginning and close of the preceding month, and quantities received during the month, including persons from whom and dates received.

Section XV: Every retail dealer in Tobacco must, on the day of receipt, enter in a book the weight of Tobacco received, the date of receipt, and the name and place of the person from whom it was received. This book must be open to inspection by the Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium or an authorized officer.

Section XVIII: All Tobacco imported, removed, kept, or found in possession for sale contrary to this Act, along with vessels, vehicles, boats, or animals used in conveyance with the owner's consent, shall be liable to confiscation. The adjudicating Officer may mitigate this penalty by commuting it to a fine not exceeding the value of the goods.
administration: The Act is administered by the Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, Officers of Customs, and Officers empowered by the Government of Bombay. Fines and confiscations are adjudicated and levied by any Magistrate of Police for the Town of Bombay.

title: THE MAJORITY ACT, 1875
purpose: To amend the law respecting the age of majority and to specify the age of majority for persons domiciled in India.
scope: It extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
key_provisions: Section 1: This Act may be called the Majority Act, 1875, and it shall come into force and have effect only on the expiration of three months from the passing thereof.
Section 1: The local extent of this Act is to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
Section 2(a): Nothing contained in this Act shall affect the capacity of any persons to act in matters of marriage, dower, divorce and adoption.
Section 2(b): Nothing contained in this Act shall affect the religion or religious rites and usages of any class of citizens of India.
Section 3(1): Every person domiciled in India shall attain the age of majority on his completing the age of eighteen years and not before.

Section 3(2): In computing the age of any person, the day on which he was born is to be included as a whole day and he shall be deemed to have attained majority at the beginning of the eighteenth anniversary of that day.
administration: information not publicly available

title: THE BENGAL BONDED WAREHOUSE ASSOCIATION ACT , 185 4
purpose: To amend Act No. V. of 1838, relating to the Bengal Bonded Warehouse Association, as desired by the Association.
scope: The Bengal Bonded Warehouse Association
key_provisions: Section I: Sections XII, XIV, XXXII, and XXXVII of Act No. V of 1838 are hereby repealed.
Section II: The business of the Association shall be managed by six Directors, three of whom shall form a quorum.
Section IV: No person shall be capable of being a Director who is not a proprietor in his own right of Five shares of the Capital Stock of the Association.

Section V: Ordinary General Meetings of proprietors shall be held at least twice yearly (second Wednesday in May and November), where Directors present a written report and balance sheet, and may declare a dividend from profits, provided it does not diminish capital.

Section VI: The Association may make Bye-laws for its proceedings, binding on its Members and Officers, provided they are approved by one extraordinary General Meeting of proprietors and confirmed by the Governor of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal.

Section VII: At any time after March 14, 1860, the Governor General of India in Council may, by order, direct the Association's dissolution, effective five years from the order date, except for purposes mentioned in Section XXXIX, Act No. V of 1838.
administration: The business of the Association is managed by six Directors, with three forming a quorum. Directors are elected at ordinary General Meetings of proprietors. Bye-laws require approval by an extraordinary General Meeting of proprietors and confirmation by the Governor of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal. The Governor General of India in Council has the power to order the dissolution of the Association.

title: THE INDIAN CHRISTIAN MARRIAGE ACT, 1872
purpose: to consolidate and amend the law relating to the solemnization in India of the marriages of persons professing the Christian religion
scope: It extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the States of Travancore-Cochin, Manipur.
key_provisions: Every marriage between persons, one or both of whom is or are a Christian or Christians, shall be solemnized in accordance with the provisions of Section 5; and any such marriage solemnized otherwise than in accordance with such provisions shall be void (Section 4).

Marriages may be solemnized in India by: (1) any person who has received episcopal ordination, according to the rules, rites, ceremonies and customs of their Church; (2) any Clergyman of the Church of Scotland, according to their Church rules, rites, ceremonies and customs; (3) any Minister of Religion licensed under this Act; (4) by, or in the presence of, a Marriage Registrar appointed under this Act; (5) by any person licensed under this Act to grant certificates of marriage between Indian Christians (Section 5).

Whenever a marriage is intended to be solemnized by a Minister of Religion licensed under this Act, one of the persons intending marriage shall give notice in writing, according to the form in the First Schedule, stating names, profession, dwelling-place, length of residence, and the church or private dwelling for solemnization (Section 12).

The father, if living, of any minor, or, if the father be dead the guardian of the person of such minor, and, in case there be no such guardian, then the mother of such minor, may give consent to the minor’s marriage, and such consent is required unless no person authorized to give such consent is resident in India (Section 19).

All marriages solemnized in India between persons one or both of whom professes or profess the Christian religion, except marriages solemnized under Part V or Part VI of this Act, shall be registered. Clergymen of the Church of England and Scotland shall keep a register according to the tabular form in the Third Schedule. Marriages solemnized by other authorized persons (Section 5(1), (2), (3)) shall be registered in duplicate in a marriage-register book and certificate (Fourth Schedule) (Sections 27, 28, 31, 32).

Every marriage between Indian Christians applying for a certificate under Part VI shall be certified if: (1) the man is not under twenty-one years and the woman is not under eighteen years; (2) neither party has a living spouse; (3) in the presence of a person licensed under Section 9 and at least two witnesses, each party declares, 'I call upon these persons here present to witness that. 1, A. B., in the presence of Almighty God, and in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, do take thee, C. D ., to be my lawful wedded wife [or husband]' or words to the like effect (Section 60).
administration: The administration of the Act involves the State Government (for licensing Ministers and persons to grant certificates, appointing Marriage Registrars, prescribing fees, and making rules), Marriage Registrars (for receiving notices, issuing certificates, and registering marriages), Ministers of Religion licensed under the Act (for solemnizing marriages and issuing certificates), Clergymen of the Church of England, Scotland, and Rome (for solemnizing and registering marriages), persons licensed under Section 9 (for granting certificates to Indian Christians), and the Registrar General of Births, Deaths and Marriages (for receiving and maintaining marriage records). High Courts and District Judges also play a role in resolving disputes related to certificate issuance.

title: The Deo Estate Act, 1886
purpose: To apply the Chutia Nagpur Encumbered Estates Act, 1876, as amended by Act V of 1884, to the Deo Estate in the Gaya District, specifically to the case of Raja Bhikam Narayan Singh Bahadur, whose immoveable property is charged with debts and liabilities, with the assent of creditors on condition that their title to receive principal and interest is not impaired.
scope: The Act applies the provisions of the Chutia Nagpur Encumbered Estates Act, 1876 (VI of 1876), as amended by Act V of 1884, to the Deo Estate in the Gaya District and to the case of Raja Bhikam Narayan Singh Bahadur and his immoveable property.
key_provisions: Section 2(1): The expressions “Commissioner”, “Deputy Commissioner” and “holder” in the Chutia Nagpur Encumbered Estates Act, 1876, shall be construed as referring to the Commissioner of the Patna division, the Collector of the Gaya district and Raja Bhikam Narayan Singh Bahadur, respectively.

Section 2(2): The Commissioner may, without any further application from Raja Bhikam Narayan Singh Bahadur and without any further notification of the consent of the Lieutenant-Governor of Bengal, publish an order appointing a manager and vesting in him the management of the whole of the immoveable property of or to which the Raja is then possessed or entitled.

Section 2(4): The principal sums, annual interest rates, and balances due on December 31, 1885, as listed in the Schedule to this Act, shall be deemed justly due to the respective creditors, save in so far as any error with respect thereto may be proved to the satisfaction of the Commissioner.

Section 2(5): The scheme prepared and approved under section 11 of the Chutia Nagpur Encumbered Estates Act, 1876, shall provide that interest at the rate of six per cent. per annum in respect of so much of the principal sum of six hundred and fifty thousand rupees as is for the time being due to the Maharaja of Darbhanga shall be paid to the Maharaja before any sum is paid thereout to any other creditor.

Section 2(8): The exercise of the power of sale conferred on the manager by section 18 of the Chutia Nagpur Encumbered Estates Act, 1876, is subject to conditions including one month’s notice to the Maharaja of Darbhanga if he is mortgagee, and restrictions on the payment of sale proceeds and the amount of property left unsold without the Maharaja's previous consent.

Section 2(9): Section 23 of the Chutia Nagpur Encumbered Estates Act, 1876, is modified such that 'any Court' replaces 'the Courts in Chutia Nagpur', and a suit relating to a claim of maintenance from the property shall not be entertained by any such Court without the previous consent of the Commissioner.
administration: The Act is administered by the Commissioner of the Patna division, the Collector of the Gaya district, and a manager appointed by the Commissioner. The Commissioner has powers related to appointing the manager, validating debts, and consenting to maintenance suits.

title: THE SIR DINSHAW MANOCKJEE PETIT ACT, 1893
purpose: An Act for settling Bonds of the Municipal Corporation of the City of Bombay producing an annual income of one lakh and twenty five thousand rupees and a Mansion-house and hereditaments called "Petit Hall" in the Island of Bombay, the property of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, Baronet, so as to accompany and support the title and dignity of a Baronet lately conferred by Her Present Majesty Queen Victoria on him for and during the term of his natural life, and from and immediately after his decease to hold to his second son, Framjee Dinshaw Petit, Esquire, and the heirs male of his body lawfully begotten, and in default of such issue with remainder to the heirs male of the body of the said Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, and for other purposes connected therewith. The Act aims to settle property in perpetuity to support the dignity of the Baronetcy title.
scope: The Act applies to specific property, including bonds of the Municipal Corporation of the City of Bombay producing an annual income of one lakh and twenty-five thousand rupees, and the Mansion-house and hereditaments called "Petit Hall" in the Island of Bombay. It governs the succession and use of this property by Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, his second son Framjee Dinshaw Petit, and the heirs male of their bodies who succeed to the Baronetcy title. The Act also establishes a Corporation of Trustees for its administration and allows for the purchase or exchange of hereditaments within the Presidency of Bombay.
key_provisions: Section 1: Arthur Frederick Cox, James MacNabb Campbell, and Charles Philip Cooper, and their successors (the Accountant-General of Bombay, the Collector of Bombay, and the Chief Presidency Magistrate of Bombay, all for the time being), are created a Corporation with perpetual succession and a common seal under the style and title of "The Trustees of the Dinshaw Manockjee Petit Baronetcy," constituted as Trustee for executing the powers and purposes of this Act.

Section 2: Framjee Dinshaw Petit and all other heirs male of the body of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit to whom the Baronetcy title descends shall take upon themselves respectively the names of "Dinshaw Manockjee Petit" in lieu of any other names and shall be called by and use those names on all occasions.

Section 3: Bonds of the Municipal Corporation of the City of Bombay, producing an annual income of not less than one lakh and twenty-five thousand rupees, shall be transferred into the name of the Corporation, who shall hold and apply the dividends, interest, and annual income for the benefit of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit during his natural life, then Framjee Dinshaw Petit during his natural life, and thereafter for the benefit of the person who for the time being has succeeded to and is in enjoyment of the Baronetcy title.

Section 6: If any Baronet refuses or neglects for one whole year, or discontinues for six consecutive calendar months, to use the names "Dinshaw Manockjee Petit," their estate or interest in the trust funds and premises shall be suspended for the remainder of their natural life, and the dividends, interest, income, possession, and rents shall devolve to the person who would have succeeded to the Baronetcy title if the defaulting person had departed this life.

Section 7: The Baronet for the time being, if in actual enjoyment of the title and using the required names, may by deed or writing, either before or after marriage, appoint to his wife or wives a jointure annuity not exceeding ten thousand rupees yearly, clear of all taxes, charges, and deductions, payable from the dividends, interest, and annual income of the settled property, commencing after his decease, by equal half-yearly payments on June 30th and December 31st.

Section 10: Neither Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, Framjee Dinshaw Petit, nor any of the heirs male of their respective bodies shall transfer, dispose of, alien, convey, charge, or encumber the settled bonds, stocks, funds, securities, Mansion-house, or hereditaments, or their income, for any greater estate, interest, or time than during his natural life, and only for such portion thereof as he shall continue to use the names of "Dinshaw Manockjee Petit"; any attempt to do so is declared void.
administration: The Act is administered by a Corporation styled "The Trustees of the Dinshaw Manockjee Petit Baronetcy." This Corporation is comprised of the Accountant-General of Bombay, the Collector of Bombay, and the Chief Presidency Magistrate of Bombay, all for the time being, and their successors. They are constituted as the Trustee for executing the powers and purposes of this Act.

title: THE PUNJAB LAWS ACT, 1872
purpose: To declare which of certain rules, laws and regulations made heretofore for the Punjab shall henceforth be in force, and to amend, consolidate or repeal others of the said rules, orders and regulations.
scope: The territories which immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the States of Punjab and Delhi, but not so as to alter the effect of any regulations made for any parts of the said territories under Statute 33 Vict. Section 1.
key_provisions: Section 5: In questions regarding succession, special property of females, betrothal, marriage, divorce, dower, adoption, guardianship, minority, bastardy, family relations, wills, legacies, gifts, partitions, or any religious usage or institution, the rule of decision shall be (1) any custom applicable to the parties concerned, not contrary to justice, equity or good conscience, and not altered, abolished, or declared void by competent authority; or (2) Muhammadan law for Muhammadans and Hindu law for Hindus, unless altered by legislative enactment, opposed to this Act, or modified by custom.
Section 6: In cases not otherwise specially provided for, the Judges shall decide according to justice, equity and good conscience.

Section 39A: The State Government may establish a system of village-watchmen or municipal-watchmen and make rules for their beats, grades, appointment, suspension, dismissal, resignation, equipment, discipline, control, supervision, powers, duties (police, sanitation, statistics), payment (including special tax collection via land-revenue process), and the exercise of authority over them by headmen or Municipal Committee members, with nomination power for headmen in village-watchmen appointments.

Section 39B: Every person is bound to render to a village-watchman, municipal watchman, or village-headman discharging police-officer duties under rules, all assistance due to a police-officer. Any person obstructing such watchman or headman may be arrested without warrant by a police-officer or by any watchman or village-headman empowered by the State Government.

Section 41: When an offence is, has been, or may reasonably be supposed to have been committed, and tracks are followed to a village, the person following such tracks may call upon any headman or village-watchman in such village to assist in carrying on the tracks.

Section 42: If a headman or watchman does not give assistance, or if village inhabitants do not afford search opportunity, or if there's reason to believe connivance at offence/escape and offenders cannot be traced beyond the village, the Magistrate of the district may, with previous sanction of the Commissioner of the Division, inflict a fine upon such village not exceeding five hundred rupees (or value of stolen property if over five hundred rupees). An appeal lies to the High Court of Punjab and Haryana. The Magistrate may award fine to injured parties and a fee (not exceeding one-fourth of stolen property value) to the tracker.
administration: The State Government is empowered to make rules, establish systems of watchmen, direct police services, and confer powers of police-officers. The Deputy Commissioner is involved in proposing and levying local taxes for police services and determining tax rates, subject to State Government approval and rules. Rules made by the State Government must be laid before the State Legislature. The High Court of Punjab and Haryana issues circulars. All rules and circulars are to be republished from time to time by the State Government.

title: THE INDIAN CONTRACT ACT, 1872
purpose: to define and amend certain parts of the law relating to contracts
scope: It extends to the whole of India; and nothing herein contained shall affect the provisions of any Statute, Act or Regulation not hereby expressly repealed, nor any usage or custom of trade, nor any incident of any contract, not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act.
key_provisions: Section 10: All agreements are contracts if they are made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not hereby expressly declared to be void.

Section 4: The communication of a proposal is complete when it comes to the knowledge of the person to whom it is made. The communication of an acceptance is complete, as against the proposer, when it is put in a course of transmission to him, so as to be out of the power of the acceptor; as against the acceptor, when it comes to the knowledge of the proposer.

Section 11: Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind, and is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject.
Section 19: When consent to an agreement is caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.

Section 73: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby, which naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, to be likely to result from the breach of it.

Section 28: Every agreement, (a) by which any party thereto is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights under or in respect of any contract, by the usual legal proceedings in the ordinary tribunals, or which limits the time within which he may thus enforce his rights; or (b) which extinguishes the rights of any party thereto, or discharges any party thereto, from any liability, under or in respect of any contract on the expiry of a specified period so as to restrict any party from enforcing his rights, is void to the extent.
administration: information not publicly available

title: The Cattle-trespass Act, 1871
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to trespasses by cattle.
scope: Extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States, and the presidency-towns and such local areas as the State Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, may from time to time exclude from its operation.
key_provisions: Pounds shall be established at such places as the Magistrate of the District, subject to the general control of the State Government, from time to time directs (Section 4). The pounds shall be under the control of the Magistrate of the District, who shall fix and may alter the rates of charge for feeding and watering impounded cattle (Section 5).

The cultivator or occupier of any land, or other specified persons, may seize cattle trespassing on such land and doing damage, and must send them or cause them to be sent within twenty-four hours to the pound established for the village (Section 10). Persons in charge of public roads, canals, embankments, and officers of police may seize cattle doing damage or straying thereon, and shall send them or cause them to be sent within twenty-four hours to the nearest pound (Section 11).

For every head of cattle impounded, pound-keepers shall levy a fine in accordance with the scale prescribed by the State Government by notification in the Official Gazette, with different scales possible for different local areas. A list of fines and feeding/watering charges shall be posted conspicuously at every pound (Section 12).

If the owner or agent claims cattle, the pound-keeper delivers them upon payment of fines and charges (Section 13). If cattle are not claimed within seven days from impounding, a notice is issued, and if still unclaimed within seven days from the date of the notice, they are sold by public auction (Section 14). Owners disputing legality of seizure may obtain cattle by depositing fines and charges (Section 15).

Any person whose cattle have been illegally seized or detained may make a complaint to the Magistrate of the District or an authorized Magistrate within ten days from the date of seizure (Section 20). The Magistrate conducts an inquiry (Section 21) and, if the seizure or detention is adjudged illegal, awards reasonable compensation not exceeding one hundred rupees and orders the release of cattle if not already released (Section 22).

Penalties include imprisonment not exceeding six months, or fine not exceeding five hundred rupees, or both, for forcibly opposing seizure or rescuing cattle (Section 24); fine not exceeding ten rupees for owners/keepers of pigs causing damage by trespass (Section 26); and fine not exceeding fifty rupees for pound-keepers failing to perform duties (Section 27).
administration: The State Government exercises general control, appoints pound-keepers, and directs registers and returns. The Magistrate of the District controls pounds, directs their establishment, fixes feeding charges, and handles complaints of illegal seizure or detention. Pound-keepers are responsible for maintaining registers, registering seizures, and caring for impounded cattle. Officers of police aid in seizures. The State Government may transfer certain functions to local authorities.

title: THE MADRAS RENT AND REVENUE SALES ACT, 1839
purpose: To empower Tahsildars to sell property distrained for arrears of rent or of revenue.
scope: The Act applies to all Tahsildars within the territories subject to the Presidency of Fort St. George. It was declared in force in the whole of the Madras Presidency, except the Scheduled Districts, and later extended to Scheduled Districts in Ganjam, Vizagapatam, and Godawari (except the Xugar Tahiq).
key_provisions: Section 2: All Tahsildars within the territories subject to the Presidency of Fort St. George shall be vested with the powers of Commissioners for the sale of property distrained for arrears of rent or of revenue.

Section 3: Tahsildars, in the exercise of their powers, shall be subject to the control and superintendence of the Collector, and shall not be subject to the authority of the Zila Judge, except in the case of any judicial proceedings.

Section 5: Tahsildars shall not be entitled to any fee or commission for selling distrained property; all such fees or commission lawfully taken by Commissioners shall be taken and carried to the account of Government.

Section 6: Tahsildars shall have authority, subject to the orders of the Collector, to delegate the powers vested in them by the second section of this Act to any public servants placed under their authority.
Section 6: The provisions of sections 3 and 5 of this Act shall apply to all public servants to whom those powers shall have been delegated in the same manner as they apply to Tahsildars.
administration: Tahsildars are vested with powers for the sale of distrained property. They are subject to the control and superintendence of the Collector and can delegate their powers to public servants under their authority, subject to the orders of the Collector. They are not subject to the Zila Judge, except in judicial proceedings.

title: THE POLICE, AGRA ACT , 185 4
purpose: To amend Regulation XI. of 1831 of the Bengal Code, as its Sections III. and VII. were found inconvenient, and to extend Regulation XI. 1831, as amended by this Act, to the whole of the Provinces of Benares.
scope: The whole of the Province of Benares.
key_provisions: Section I: Sections III. and VII., Regulation XI. 1831 of the Bengal Code are hereby repealed.

Section II: Wherever any Tehseeldar shall have Police jurisdiction under the provisions of Section II. of Regulation XI. 1831, every Darogah of Police hereafter appointed within the local limits of the police jurisdiction of such Tehseeldar, shall be subordinate to, and subject to the control of such Tehseeldar, in his capacity of Chief Police Thannadar.
Section III: Regulation XI. 1831, as amended by this Act, shall extend to the whole of the Province of Benares.
Section III: All powers vested by Regulation XI. 1831 in the Governor General in Council, may be exercised by the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces.
administration: Tehseeldars, in their capacity of Chief Police Thannadar, exercise police jurisdiction and control Darogahs of Police. Powers previously vested in the Governor General in Council may be exercised by the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces.

title: The Moorshedabad Act, 1891
purpose: To confirm and give effect to an Indenture between the Secretary of State and the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad, Amir-ul-Omrah.
scope: The Act applies to the confirmation and effectuation of an indenture concerning the position, dignity, and maintenance of the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad, including specific moveable and immoveable properties, annual payments, and the relinquishment of the title of Nawab Nazim of Bengal, Behar and Orissa.
key_provisions: Section 2. Confirmation of indenture of March, 1891: "The said indenture is hereby confirmed."

Section 3. Additions to schedule to indenture: "The Governor General in Council, by notification in the Gazette of India, may in his discretion, on the written request of the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad for the time being, add... to the schedules of immoveable property... any additional immoveable property which may be acquired from time to time for the maintenance of the position and dignity of the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad for the time being."

Section 4. Limitation for claims to scheduled immoveable property: "No right to any immoveable property mentioned in any of the schedules to the said indenture... shall... be acquired by any person by adverse possession or assertion of title unless such adverse possession or assertion of title is found to have existed for sixty years."

Annual Payment Covenant: The Secretary of State and his successors "shall and will... pay or cause to be paid annually for ever from the revenues of the Government of India unto the said Nawab Bahadoor and his lineal heirs male in perpetuity the sum of rupees two lakhs and thirty thousand by equal monthly instalments of rupees nineteen thousand one hundred and sixty-six ten annas and eight pies by monthly instalments on or before the 5th day of each and every succeeding month from the Treasury of the Government of India at Berhampore."

Property Inalienability: "The said Nawab Bahadoor shall not nor shall any of his successors in the said titles sell mortgage devise or alienate the said properties respectively or any of them otherwise than by lease or demise for a term not exceeding 21 years and under a rent without bonus or salamee."

Enforcement for Mismanagement/Alienation: "In case the said Nawab Bahadoor or any of his lineal heirs male successors to the titles shall at any time in contravention of the terms of these presents attempt to sell mortgage devise or alienate... or shall by a course of extravagance or by waste or mismanagement... it shall be lawful for the Secretary of State for the time being at his discretion to enter into and upon the said immoveable properties and to hold and take possession thereof and receive and take the rents issues and profits thereof and also to take and retain the said monthly sum of Rs. 19,166-10-8 payable from the Government Treasury at Berhampore..."
administration: The Secretary of State for India in Council and the Governor General in Council are responsible for the administration of the Act and the provisions of the indenture. The Governor General in Council handles additions to property schedules, while the Secretary of State manages annual payments, property oversight, and enforcement actions, with the Treasury of the Government of India at Berhampore involved in payments and deductions.

title: THE INDIAN RESERVE FORCES ACT, 1888
purpose: To regulate the Indian Reserve Forces and to provide for their Government, discipline and regulation.
scope: Applies to the Indian Reserve Forces, which consist of the Regular Reserve and the Supplementary Reserve (Section 2). Persons belonging to the Indian Reserve Forces are liable to serve beyond the limits of India as well as within those limits (Section 3). The Act has been extended to and brought into force in Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Lakshadweep, and Pondicherry.
key_provisions: The Indian Reserve Forces shall consist of the Regular Reserve and the Supplementary Reserve (Section 2).

The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules and orders for the government, discipline and regulation of the Indian Reserve Forces (Section 4(1)). Every such rule or order shall be laid before each House of Parliament for a total period of thirty days, and may be modified or annulled by both Houses (Section 4(2)).

A person belonging to the Indian Reserve Forces shall be subject to military law in the same manner and to the same extent as a person belonging to the Regular Army, subject to rules and orders made under Section 4 (Section 5).

Persons belonging to the Indian Reserve Forces who fail to attend as required, fail to comply with rules/orders, or fraudulently obtain pay, are liable on conviction by a court-martial to punishment (other than death, transportation, or imprisonment exceeding one year as per Army Act, 1950), or on conviction by a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class, to imprisonment up to six months for a first offence and up to one year for subsequent offences (Section 6(1)).

Employers have a duty to reinstate persons belonging to the Indian Reserve Forces in their civil employment upon termination of training, muster, or army service, under conditions not less favourable than before (Section 7(1)). If an employer refuses or deems reinstatement impracticable, either party may refer the matter to an authority prescribed by rules, which can order reinstatement, exemption, or compensation up to six months' remuneration (Proviso to Section 7(1)).

Persons called up for training, muster, or army service shall continue to have rights under any provident fund, superannuation fund, or other employee benefit scheme connected with their relinquished employment, for the duration of their service and until reinstatement, as prescribed by rules made under this Act (Section 8).
administration: The Central Government is empowered to make rules and orders for the government, discipline, and regulation of the Indian Reserve Forces (Section 4(1)). These rules and orders are subject to parliamentary oversight (Section 4(2)). Specific officers may be appointed by rules or orders for administrative tasks such as signing certificates (Section 6(2)), and an authority prescribed by rules handles disputes regarding reinstatement in civil employment (Section 7(1) proviso).

title: THE REVENUE RECOVERY ACT, 1890
purpose: to make better provision for recovering certain public demands.
scope: Extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (as amended), and applies to the recovery of arrears of land-revenue or sums recoverable as arrears of land-revenue. It also covers the recovery in India of certain public demands arising beyond India (Section 8) and land revenues, etc., accruing in Burma or Pakistan (Section 9).
key_provisions: Recovery of public demands by enforcement of processes in other districts: Where an arrear of land-revenue is payable by a defaulter having property in another district, the Collector may send a certificate in the form as nearly as may be of the Schedule, stating the defaulter's identification and the amount due. The Collector of the other district shall, on receiving the certificate, proceed to recover the amount as if it were an arrear of land-revenue which had accrued in his own district (Section 3).

Remedy available to person denying liability: When proceedings are taken for recovery, a person denying liability may pay the amount under protest made in writing and institute a suit for repayment in a Civil Court having jurisdiction in the local area where the office of the Collector who made the certificate is situate (Section 4).

Recovery by Collectors of sums recoverable as arrears of revenue by other public officers or by local authorities: Where any sum is recoverable as an arrear of land-revenue by any public officer (other than a Collector) or by a local authority, the Collector of the district in which the office of that officer or authority is situate shall, on request, recover the sum as if it were an arrear of land-revenue which had accrued in his own district, and may send a certificate to another district (Section 5).

Property liable to sale under this Act: When a Collector receives a certificate, he may issue a proclamation prohibiting the transfer or charging of any immovable property belonging to the defaulter. Any private alienation of the property made after the issue of the proclamation and before its withdrawal shall be void as against the Government and any person who may purchase the property at a sale held for recovery (Section 6).

Duty of Collectors to remit moneys collected in certain cases: Where a Collector receives a certificate under this Act from a Collector of another State or a Collector in Pakistan or Burma, he shall remit any sum recovered by him by virtue of that certificate to that Collector, after deducting his expenses in connection with the matter (Section 10).
administration: The Act is administered primarily by 'Collectors,' defined as the chief officer in charge of the land-revenue administration of a district, who are responsible for issuing and acting upon recovery certificates. In some states, 'Certificate Officers' may exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of a Collector (e.g., Assam Act 16 of 1971, s. 2). State Governments may also make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act (e.g., Uttar Pradesh Act 11 of 1965, s. 6).

title: THE PARTITION OF REVENUE -PAYING ESTATES ACT , 1863
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the partition of estates paying revenue to Government in the North -Western Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal.
scope: This Act extends only to such parts of the North -Western Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal as are subject to the general Regulations of that Presidency. It may be extended, by order of the Local Government, either wholly or in part, to any Non -Regulation Province under such Government (Section LIX). The Act applies to the partition of estates paying Revenue to Government, and its provisions may be applied to the partition of any estate held free from the payment of Government Revenue by order of the Local Government (Section LI).
key_provisions: Recorded proprietors of a joint undivided estate paying Revenue to Government, or any portion thereof, are entitled to claim partition and must apply in writing to the Collector of the District (Section III, IV). The application must be signed and specify the nature of the tenure, names of all co-sharers, their respective shares, and the desired mode of partition (Section V).

If an objection to partition raises a question of title or proprietary right, the Collector may either decline the application until a competent Court determines the dispute, or inquire into the merits of the objection. The procedure for such inquiry shall be that laid down in Act XIV of 1882 for the trial of original suits, and the Collector may refer questions to arbitration under Chapter XXXVII of the Code of Civil Procedure (Section VIII). Decisions by the Collector on rights are appealable to the District or Sadr Court (Section IX).

After inquiry, the Collector shall offer parties the option of making a private partition and allotment of public revenue. If this fails, parties may refer the partition and revenue apportionment to arbitrators appointed by them or, if they cannot agree, by the Collector. If private agreement or arbitration fails, the Collector shall appoint an Officer to make the partition (Sections XVIII, XIX, XXV).

The expense of making the partition, including allowances for establishment, measurement, survey, and paper preparation, shall be fixed by the Collector. The amount is to be paid under rules laid down by the Board of Revenue with the sanction of the Local Government, and in default of payment, may be realized under rules for recovering arrears of rent or revenue (Section XIV).

The Officer appointed to make the partition must ensure that the estates formed are as compact as possible (Section XXXV). In selecting villages or lands for each separate estate, considerations include situation, vicinity of roads/railways/rivers/canals, soil quality, waste land, water depth, tanks, wells, embankments, and other local circumstances affecting value (Section XXXVII). Specific rules apply to dwelling-houses (Section XXXVIII), tanks/wells/water-courses/embankments (Section XXXIX), and places of worship (Section XL).

The Commissioner may confirm or modify the partition proposed by the Collector, and this decision is subject to appeal to the Board of Revenue (Section XLIII). Upon receiving the final order, the Collector publishes it, specifies the date from which each estate is separate, enters them in the Register of Estates paying Revenue to Government, and gives the proprietors possession (Section XLIV).
administration: The Collector of the District is primarily responsible for carrying out partitions under this Act, subject to the general direction and control of the Commissioner of the Division and the Board of Revenue (Section LII). Orders passed by a Collector, unless otherwise provided and not being decisions under Section IX, are open to revision by the superior Revenue Authorities (Section LIII). Powers vested in a Collector may also be exercised by a Deputy Collector or other Officer vested with the full powers of a Collector, subject to the control of the Collector of the District (Section LIV). The Board of Revenue is guided by orders or instructions from the Local Government (Section LVII).

title: THE NORTHERN INDIA CANAL AND DRAINAGE ACT, 1873
purpose: To regulate irrigation, navigation and drainage in Northern India, and to amend the law relating to irrigation, navigation and drainage in the said territories.
scope: The Act extends to Uttar Pradesh and the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the States of Punjab and Delhi, and applies to all lands whether permanently settled, temporarily settled, or free from revenue.
key_provisions: Section 5: The State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, declare that the water of any river, stream, lake, or natural collection of still water will be applied or used for any existing or projected canal or drainage-work after a day named in the notification, not being earlier than three months from the date thereof.

Section 16: Any person desiring to use canal-water may apply in writing to the Divisional or Sub-Divisional Canal-officer to construct or improve a water-course at their cost. The application must state the works, estimated cost, or willingness to pay actual cost, and payment method. Upon assent of the Superintending Canal-officer and attestation before the Collector, applicants are jointly and severally liable for costs, which are recoverable as arrears of land-revenue if unpaid.

Section 21 & 22: Any person desiring the construction of a new water-course may apply in writing to the Divisional Canal-officer. If the officer deems construction expedient and the application statements true, he shall call for a deposit, cause inquiry into alignment, mark out the necessary land, and publish a notice in every village through which the water-course is proposed to be taken, sending a copy to the Collector of every district concerned.

Section 36 & 37: Rates for canal-water supplied for irrigation to occupiers of land, called the 'occupier’s rate,' shall be determined by rules made by the State Government. Additionally, an 'owner’s rate' may be imposed by State Government rules on owners of canal-irrigated lands for the benefit derived from such irrigation.

Section 70: Whoever, without proper authority and voluntarily, damages, alters, enlarges, or obstructs any canal or drainage-work; interferes with water supply or flow; neglects water-course maintenance; corrupts canal water; navigates contrary to rules; fails to supply labourers as required under Part VIII; destroys or moves level-marks or water-gauges; or violates any rule made under this Act, shall be liable, on conviction before a Magistrate, to a fine not exceeding fifty rupees, or to imprisonment not exceeding one month, or to both.
administration: The State Government may appoint officers (including Canal-officers, Commissioners, and Collectors) by notification in the Official Gazette, declaring their powers, duties, and local limits. All officers mentioned in section 3, clause (7) (Canal-officers), are subject to the orders of officers directed by the State Government. The State Government also has the power to make, alter, and cancel rules to regulate officer proceedings, appeals, procedures, charges, and generally to carry out the Act's provisions, with such rules being published in the Official Gazette to have the force of law.

title: THE COURT-FEES ACT, 1870
purpose: To regulate and levy fees in High Courts, Courts of Small Causes, Mufassal Courts, and public offices for various legal documents and proceedings, including those related to probates, letters of administration, and certificates of administration.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. It came into force on the first day of April, 1870.
key_provisions: Levy of fees in High Courts and Presidency Small Cause Courts (Sections 3, 4): Fees are chargeable on documents filed, exhibited, or recorded in High Courts (in their original, extraordinary, appellate, reference, or revision jurisdictions) and in Presidency Small Cause Courts, as specified in the first or second schedule to this Act.

Procedure in case of difference as to necessity or amount of fee (Section 5): Differences arising in High Courts are referred to the taxing-officer (whose decision is final, unless it's a question of general importance, then referred to the Chief Justice or appointed Judge). Differences in Courts of Small Causes are referred to the Clerk of the Court (whose decision is final, unless it's a question of general importance, then referred to the first Judge of such Court).

Computation of fees payable in certain suits (Section 7): Fees are computed based on the amount claimed for money suits, ten times the annual amount for maintenance/annuities, market-value for movable property, or the plaintiff's valuation for property of no market-value, declaratory decrees, injunctions, easements, or accounts. For possession of land, houses, and gardens, value is determined by revenue multiples or market-value.

Refund of fee where court refers parties to dispute settlement (Section 16): Where the court refers the parties to the suit to any mode of settlement of dispute under section 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908), the plaintiff is entitled to a certificate from the court authorizing him to receive back from the Collector the full amount of the fee paid in respect of such plaint.

Provision for case where too low a court-fee has been paid on probates, etc. (Section 19E): If a person paid too low a court-fee on probate or letters of administration due to under-estimation, the Chief Controlling Revenue-authority may cause the document to be duly stamped upon payment of the full original court-fee plus a penalty (five times if produced within one year, twenty times if after one year from grant). The penalty may be remitted if the application is made within six months of discovering the mistake and without fraudulent intent.

Collection of fees by stamps and rules for their management (Sections 25, 26, 27): All fees chargeable under this Act shall be collected by stamps. The stamps used shall be impressed or adhesive, or partly both, as the appropriate Government directs. The appropriate Government may make rules for regulating the supply, number, renewal of damaged/spoiled stamps, and keeping accounts of all stamps used, with the concurrence of the Chief Justice for High Court stamps.
administration: The administration of the Act involves the 'appropriate Government' (Central or State, depending on the officer), which directs stamp types, makes rules for stamp supply, renewal, accounts, and sales, and has the power to reduce or remit fees. High Courts make rules for process fees and, with the Chief Justice's concurrence, for stamps used in High Courts. District Judges and Magistrates fix the number of peons for process service. The Chief Controlling Revenue-authority handles matters related to probates and letters of administration and fixes peons in Revenue Courts. Collectors are involved in refunds and inquiries regarding property valuation for probates. Taxing-officers and Chief Justices (for High Courts) and Clerks of Court and First Judges (for Small Cause Courts) resolve disputes concerning the necessity or amount of fees.

title: THE LAWS LOCAL EXTENT ACT, 1874
purpose: To declare the local extent of certain Acts passed by the Governor General of India in Council, the Legislative Council of India, and the Council of the Governor General of India assembled for the purpose of making Laws and Regulations; and to consolidate the laws relating to the local extent of certain Acts and Regulations in the Presidencies of Fort St. George and Bombay, and in the Lower and the North-Western Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal.
scope: The Act applies to the local extent of certain enactments across India, specifically excluding "the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States" and the "Scheduled Districts" (territories mentioned in the sixth schedule). It details the application of enactments in the Presidencies of Fort St. George and Bombay, and the Lower and North-Western Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal, with exceptions for their respective Scheduled Districts. It also contains savings clauses regarding the towns of Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay, and certain Parganas in the Mirzapur and Benares districts.
key_provisions: Section 1: This Act may be called the Laws Local Extent Act, 1874.
Section 2: In this Act the expression “Scheduled Districts” means the territories mentioned in the sixth schedule hereto annexed.

Section 3: The Acts mentioned in the first schedule hereto annexed are now in force in the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States and the Scheduled Districts.

Section 4: The enactments mentioned in the second schedule hereto annexed are now in force throughout the whole of the territories now subject to the government of the Governor of Fort St. George in Council, except the Scheduled Districts subject to such government.

Section 8(a): Nothing herein contained shall bar the power of the Central Government or the State Government under any law for the time being in force, to extend to any place any Act mentioned in the said first schedule.
Section 8(j): Nothing herein contained shall extend to any of the towns of Calcutta, Madras and Bombay any, law not now in force therein.
administration: information not publicly available

title: THE BOMABY RENT -FREE ESTATES ACT, 1852
purpose: To provide means for trying and determining claims against Government on account of Inams and other Estates wholly or partially exempt from payment of Land Revenue in certain districts of the Bombay Presidency, where existing civil courts and regulations were inadequate for such adjudication.
scope: The Act applies to claims against Government regarding Inams and other estates wholly or partially exempt from payment of Land Revenue in the Territories of the Deccan Kandeish, Southern Mahratta Country, and other districts recently annexed to the Bombay Presidency, specifically those not brought under the General Regulations of Government by Regulation XXVIII. of 1827 of the Bombay Code.
key_provisions: The Governor of Bombay in Council may appoint an Inam Commissioner with Assistants and subordinate establishment in any Zillah or division not under the General Regulations of Government by Regulation XXVIII. of 1827 (Section II).
Claims to exempt lands or interests shall be adjudicated and titles determined according to the Rules in Schedule B annexed to this Act (Section IV).

Each Inam Commissioner and his Assistants shall have the same authority as ordinary Civil Courts to procure witness attendance, take evidence, and inflict penalties for not giving evidence, false testimony, resistance of process, and contempts (Section V).

Orders of Assistant Commissioners are appealable to the Inam Commissioner, and orders of the Inam Commissioner are appealable to the Governor of Bombay in Council, whose orders are final. Appeals must be made by petition within one hundred days from the decree date, accompanied by a copy of the decree (Schedule A, Rule 2 and Rule 14).

Lands held under a sunnud declaring them hereditary shall be continued according to its terms, provided the grant was made or recognized by competent authority to alienate Government Revenue in perpetuity, and does not involve illegal conditions or has not been revoked (Schedule B, Rule 2, Provisions 1st, 2nd, 3rd).

Lands uninterruptedly held as wholly or partially exempt from assessment for sixty years before the introduction of the British Government, and then in the authorized possession of a grandson in male descent or male heir of the body of such grandson of the original grantee, shall continue to be so held as long as a male heir of the body of the incumbent at the introduction of British Government exists, tracing lineage through male heirs only (Schedule B, Rule 3).
administration: The Act is administered by an Inam Commissioner and his Assistants, appointed by the Governor of Bombay in Council. The Governor in Council holds final appellate authority, issues instructions, prescribes methods for executing decisions, can relax rules, and interprets the rules. Decisions are carried into execution by the Collector or Chief Revenue Authority of the District at the requisition of the Inam Commissioner or his Assistant (Sections II, III, V, VII, Schedule A Rules 1, 2, 13, Schedule B Rule 11).

title: THE BOMBAY REVENUE JURISDICTION ACT, 1876
purpose: To limit the jurisdiction of the Civil Courts throughout the Bombay Presidency in matters relating to the Land-revenue, and for other purposes, as it was expedient that the jurisdiction of all the Civil Courts in the said Presidency should be limited.
scope: The Act extends to all the State of Maharashtra, but does not affect (a) any suit regarding the assessment or collection of revenue on land situate in the City of Bombay, or (b) any provisions of Bombay Acts 5 of 1862 and 6 of 1862, or of Act 21 of 1881 or Act 23 of 1871. Civil Courts in the Districts mentioned in the Second Schedule (Ahmedabad, Kaira, Broach, Surat, Tanna, Colaba, Ratnagiri, Kanara) may exercise jurisdiction over certain claims against the Government as per laws in force on March 28, 1876.
key_provisions: No Civil Court shall exercise jurisdiction as to claims against the Government relating to any property appertaining to the office of any hereditary officer appointed or recognized under Bombay Act No. 3 of 1874, or any other law for the time being in force, or of any other village-officer or servant, or claims to perform the duties of any such officer or servant, or in respect of any injury caused by exclusion from such office or service (Section 4(a)).

Civil Courts are not prevented from entertaining suits against the Government to contest the amount claimed, or paid under protest, or recovered, as land-revenue on the ground that such amount is in excess of the amount authorized by the State Government, or that such amount had previous to such claim, payment, or recovery been satisfied, in whole or in part, or that the plaintiff, or the person whom he represents, is not the person liable for such amount (Section 5(a)).

No Civil Court shall entertain any suit against the Government on account of any act or omission of any Revenue-officer unless the plaintiff first proves that, previously to bringing his suit, he has presented all such appeals allowed by the law for the time being in force, as within the period of limitation allowed for bringing such suit, it was possible to present (Section 11).

The State Government may refer questions arising in the trial or investigation of any suit, claim or objection, which but for this Act might have been tried by a Civil Court, for the decision of the High Court, by causing a statement of the question to be prepared (Section 12). The High Court shall fix an early day for hearing, cause notice to be placed in the Court-house, and allow parties to appear in person or by advocates or pleaders.

If a Civil Judge doubts whether he is precluded by this Act from taking cognizance of a suit or appeal, he may refer the matter to the High Court (Section 13). The High Court may order the Judge making the reference either to proceed with the case or to return the plaint.

When a suit is brought in any District Court against the Government or a Revenue officer, and the Government undertakes the defence, the State Government may, by certificate signed by a Secretary, require that the suit be tried by the District Judge himself (not an Assistant Judge) and that its trial have precedence over other pending civil proceedings (Section 16).
administration: The Act involves the State Government, Revenue officers (including the Collector of the District), Civil Courts (including Civil Judges, District Judges, and Assistant Judges), and the High Court (with the Chief Justice directing Bench composition for references) in its administration and application.

title: THE PUNJAB TENANCY ACT, 1887
purpose: to amend the law relating to the tenancy of land in the Punjab
scope: the whole of the territories (including the pargana of Spiti) for the time being administered by the Lieutenant – Governor of the Punjab, expect the Hazara district
key_provisions: A tenant who at the commencement of this Act has for more than two generations in the male line of descent through a grandfather or grand-uncle and for a period of not less than twenty years been occupying land paying no rent thereof beyond the amount of the land-revenue thereof and the rates and cesses for the time being chargeable thereon, has a right of occupancy in the land so occupied (Section 5(1)(a)). A tenant recorded in a record-of-rights sanctioned before October 21, 1868, as having a right of occupancy in land continuously occupied since the record's preparation, shall be deemed to have such a right unless contrary is established by a competent Court decree (Section 6).

If either the landlord or the tenant neglects to attend for division or appraisement of produce, or if there is a dispute, a Revenue-officer may, on application, appoint a referee to divide or appraise the produce (Section 17). The referee makes the division/appraisement according to instructions, gives notice to parties, and may proceed exparte if a party fails to attend (Section 18). The referee's record is submitted to the Revenue-officer, who confirms or varies the division/appraisement and orders on costs (Section 19).

A landlord may apply to a Revenue-officer for ejectment of a tenant against whom a decree for arrear of rent remains unsatisfied (Section 43, Section 42(a)). The Revenue-officer serves a notice stating the decree date and amount due, informing the tenant that failure to pay within fifteen days from receipt will result in ejectment (Section 44(1)). If not paid, ejectment is ordered unless good cause is shown (Section 44(2)). For a tenant from year to year (Section 42(b)), a notice of ejectment is served (not after November 15), requiring vacation by May 1 or institution of a suit in a Revenue Court within two months to contest liability (Section 45(1), (2), (3)).

A tenant having a right of occupancy under section 5 may transfer that right by sale, gift, or mortgage. The tenant must serve notice of intention on the landlord through a Revenue-officer and defer the transfer for one month from the date of service (Section 53(1), (2)). Within this month, the landlord may claim to purchase the right at a value fixed by a Revenue-officer on application (Section 53(3)).

In suits by a tenant to contest ejectment or by a landlord to eject or enhance rent, the Court directs the tenant to file a claim for compensation for improvements or disturbance (Section 70(1)). If ejectment or enhancement is decreed, the Court determines compensation and stays execution until the landlord pays the amount (less arrears/costs) into Court (Section 70(2)). Alternatively, a tenant served with an ejectment notice under Section 44 or 45 may apply to the Revenue-officer to determine compensation, and ejectment is stayed until the landlord pays the determined amount (Section 71).

The following suits shall be instituted in and heard and determined by Revenue Courts: Suits between landlord and tenant for enhancement or reduction of rent under section 24; Suits between landlord and tenant for addition to or abatement of rent under section 28 or for commutation of rent; Suits under section 34 for the determination of rent or other sum on the expiration of the term of an assessment of land-revenue (Section 77(3), First Group).
administration: The general superintendence and control over all other Revenue-officers and Revenue Courts is vested in the Financial Commissioner. Subject to the Financial Commissioner's control, a Commissioner controls all other Revenue-officers and Revenue Courts in their division. Subject to the Commissioner's control, a Collector controls all other Revenue-officers and Revenue Courts in their district. The Local Government may confer powers of Financial Commissioner, Commissioner, Collector, or Assistant Collector on any person by notification (Sections 75, 78, 105).

title: THE MADRAS DISTRICT POLICE ACT, 1859
purpose: to make the Police Force throughout the Madras Presidency a more efficient instrument at the disposal of the Magistrate for the prevention and detection of crime, and to re-organize the Police Force and improve the condition of the Village Police
scope: The operation of this Act shall be extended to all districts designated as the "General Police District" by notification published in the Official Gazette by the Governor in Council (Section I, LV). It shall have full force in any part of the Madras Presidency except within the limits of the Supreme Court (Section XXXIII).
key_provisions: **Constitution and Management of the Police Force (Sections VIII, IX, X, XI):** The entire Police establishment of the Madras Presidency is deemed one Police Force, formally enrolled, and constituted as ordered by the Governor in Council with the sanction of the Governor General of India in Council. The Inspector-General, subject to Governor in Council approval, frames orders and regulations for the Force's government, distribution, classification, rank, service, inspection, equipment, and intelligence. Appointment of Police Officers rests with the Inspector-General and Deputy Superintendents, who may dismiss, suspend, or fine officers up to one month's pay. Every appointed person receives a certificate (Form A) under the Inspector-General's seal, vesting them with Police Officer powers, functions, and privileges, which must be surrendered upon suspension, dismissal, or removal.

**Powers of Arrest without Warrant (Section XXII):** Police Officers are authorized to arrest without warrant persons charged on credible information or suspected of grave crimes; persons charged with recently committed aggravated assault where a warrant could not have been issued due to recent commission; persons committing or attempting a breach of the peace in view who refuse to desist; persons found injuring public buildings, roads, tanks, and water channels or committing any other punishable offence (unless slight and no absconding risk); vagrants disturbing public peace or suspected of crime, and persons whose name and residence are unknown or found loitering by night unable to give a satisfactory account; persons assaulting, resisting, or obstructing a Police Officer; persons escaping from legal custody; and persons charged with injury to person or property who refuse to give their name and residence or give a false one (for identification purposes only).

**Execution of Criminal Processes (Sections XXXII, XXXIII):** All summonses, warrants, search warrants, warrants of commitment for trial, or orders for the escort and conveyance of prisoners, and all other processes issued by any Officer in any Criminal proceeding, shall be directed and delivered to Officers of the Police alone; and such processes shall be served and executed by them and none others. An Officer receiving such a process shall endorse it to one or more Police Officers for execution, who then possess the same powers, privileges, and protection as if originally named. Such processes must be executed with secrecy and dispatch and have full force throughout the Madras Presidency, except within Supreme Court limits, without further formality or local endorsement.

**Regulation of Public Order and Nuisances (Sections XLVIII, XLIX):** The Superintendent and Superior Officers of Police may, as occasion requires, direct the conduct of all assemblies and processions in public roads, streets, or thoroughfares, prescribe routes and times, keep order in public places, prevent obstructions, and regulate the use of music in streets during native festivals and ceremonies. They may also direct all crowds of twelve or more persons to disperse when there is reason to apprehend any breach of the peace. Persons committing specified offences in streets, roads, thoroughfares, or passages within town limits (e.g., slaughtering cattle, furious riding, cruelty to animals, obstructing passengers, exposing goods for sale, throwing dirt, public drunkenness, indecent exposure, neglecting dangerous places) are liable to fines or imprisonment, and Police Officers may take into custody without warrant any person who within view commits any such offence.

**Police Superannuation Fund (Section XII):** A "Police Superannuation Fund" shall be established through deductions from the pay of every Police Officer (not exceeding one anna in the Rupee for those not entitled to Uncovenanted Service Pension Rules), monies from pay stoppages during absence, fines imposed on Police Officers for misconduct, fines imposed by Magistrates on drunken persons or for assaults on Police Officers, and proceeds from the sale of worn clothing or other miscellaneous sources permitted by the Governor in Council. These sums shall be invested as directed by the Governor in Council, and the accumulated interest and dividends shall be applied to superannuation or retiring allowances, or gratuities, under such rules as may be passed by the said Governor in Council.
administration: The superintendence of the police throughout the General Police District shall vest in, and be exercised by the Governor in Council (Section IV). The administration of the Police is vested in an Officer styled the Inspector-General of Police for the Presidency of Madras, and in such Subordinates as the Governor in Council appoints and removes (Section V). The Inspector-General is a Justice of the Peace and has full powers of a Magistrate throughout the General Police District, subject to Governor in Council orders (Section VII). The Governor in Council may also vest District Superintendents with magisterial powers (Section VII). The Inspector-General, subject to Governor in Council approval, frames orders and regulations for the Force (Section IX). Appointment and dismissal of Police Officers rest with the Inspector-General and Deputy Superintendents under rules sanctioned by the Governor in Council (Section X).

title: THE PUNJAB LAND -REVENUE ACT, 1887
purpose: To amend and declare the law in force in the Punjab with respect to the making and maintenance of records-of-rights in land, the assessment and collection of land-revenue, and other matters relating to land and the liabilities incident thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the territories for the time being administered by the Lieutenant-Governor of the Punjab, including the pargana of Spiti. It does not apply to land occupied as the site of a town or village and not assessed to land-revenue, except as necessary for the record, recovery, and administration of village-cesses.
key_provisions: Record-of-rights and Annual Records (Sections 31, 33, 34): Establishes a record-of-rights for each estate, including details of landowners, tenants, interests, payments, customs, and a map. The Collector causes annual records to be prepared by the patwari, amended with mutations reported by persons acquiring rights (within three months) or identified by the patwari, and verified by a Revenue Officer.

Assessment of Land-Revenue (Sections 48, 51, 52): All land is liable for land-revenue. A general re-assessment requires the previous sanction of the Governor General in Council. A Revenue Officer determines and announces the assessment for each estate (Section 51). Landowners or assignees may petition for reconsideration within thirty days from the date of announcement (Section 52).

Recovery of Arrears of Land-Revenue (Section 67): Arrears of land-revenue may be recovered by processes including writ of demand, arrest and detention of the defaulter (up to 10 days by Revenue Officer, up to 1 month in civil jail by Collector), distress and sale of movable property/crops, transfer of holding, attachment of estate/holding, annulment of assessment, or sale of the estate/holding.

Partition of Land and Tenancies (Sections 111, 113, 117): Any joint owner of land or joint tenant with occupancy rights may apply to a Revenue Officer for partition of their share (Section 111). The Revenue Officer issues notice to co-sharers and landlords (Section 113). Disputes as to title may be determined by the Revenue Officer acting as a competent Court, with specific procedures and appeal rights (Section 117).
Exclusion of Civil Courts Jurisdiction (Section 158): Civil Courts are excluded from jurisdiction in matters within the jurisdiction of Revenue Officers.
administration: The administration is carried out by Revenue Officers, comprising the Financial Commissioner, Commissioners, Collectors (Deputy Commissioners), and Assistant Collectors (first and second grade, which include Assistant Commissioners, Extra Assistant Commissioners, Tahsildars, and Naib-tahsildars). The Financial Commissioner is appointed and removed by the Local Government with the Governor General in Council's sanction and exercises general superintendence and control over other Revenue Officers, subject to the Local Government. Commissioners control Revenue Officers in their division, and Collectors control Revenue Officers in their district. Village officers (chief-headman, headman, patwari) also have duties under the Act.

title: THE POLICE ACT, 1861
purpose: To re-organise the police and to make it a more efficient instrument for the prevention and detection of crime.
scope: This Act shall not by its own operation take effect in any presidency, State or place.
